editor_notes.source_verification: Both source snapshots read in full: source-0.html.gz (tiobe.com, TIOBE Index for July 2026 page) and source-1.html.gz (infoworld.com, Paul Krill's July 6, 2026 article). The single automated allowlist warning (tiobe.com) is a false positive — tiobe.com is the article's own primary subject (TIOBE reporting on itself), not a third-party citation needing allowlist clearance; this mirrors the identical false-positive finding and upgrade in the May 2026 TIOBE review (src/content/reviews/2026-05/2026-05-19T09-40-10Z_tiobe-may-2026-r-matches-all-time-high-as-sas-face_review.json). infoworld.com is already in config/source_allowlist.txt.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific claim checked against the snapshots and confirmed: Rust position 10 (Jul 2026) vs 18 (Jul 2025), rating 1.34% / +0.33pp (source-0 table row, matches InfoWorld's '1.34% rating, Rust is ranked 10th'); Delphi/Object Pascal displaced from 10th to 11th, 1.29% / -0.48pp (source-0 table); all three Jansen quotes verbatim in source-0 and independently corroborated verbatim in source-1 ('strong focus on memory safety while still generating extremely fast code'; 'is widely regarded as a direct competitor to C and C++...often considered less safe'; 'the C and C++ communities are actively working on making their languages safer'; 'Time will tell whether these efforts will pay off in time'); Python #1 18.94% / -8.03pp (source-0); C 2nd at 10.86% swapping with C++ 3rd at 9.12% (source-0 table shows C moved 3->2, C++ moved 2->3); Java/C#/JavaScript held 4th/5th/6th (source-0); SQL 13th->8th at 1.71% and R 15th->9th at 1.69% (source-0); Pypl index Rust 9th at 2.06% behind Python/Java/C-C++/R/JavaScript/Objective-C/PHP/C# (source-1 Pypl list, order matches exactly); 25th-anniversary quotes about C/C++/Java, Python, and C# top-five timing verbatim in source-0; Programming Language Flowchart 'next week' quote verbatim in source-0 (InfoWorld's own text says 'this week or next week' but the article correctly quotes TIOBE's own commentary, which says 'next week'); 'Last month, we reported that Rust was setting new records' verbatim in source-0; TIOBE ratings methodology (Google, Bing, Amazon, Wikipedia) matches source-1; TIOBE's own caveat about not indicating 'the best choice for a particular project or application' verbatim in source-0. Cross-checked the internal link to the May 2026 TIOBE article and confirmed its stated Rust figures (#15, 1.14%) match that article's published text. No fabrications, no hallucinated quotes, no misattributions found.

Verdict upgraded from automated APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE — the sole automated finding is an allowlist false positive for the article's own primary source (tiobe.com), consistent with the precedent set in the May 2026 TIOBE review.
